children: Aanya Thakur Mumbai: Indian shoppers are finding fresh excuses to click 'Buy Now', thanks to savvy marketers. The latest is 11.11, or Singles' Day, on November 11, when brands such as H&M, Puma, Bath & Body Works and Levi's, along with retailers like Shoppers Stop, offered discounts to turn the Chinese occasion into a shopping event here too. With retailers looking to beat the usual post-Diwali consumption lull, marketers are creating new shopping festivals - popular in the West - to keep consumers spending.

Singles' Day and Thanksgiving are joining the likes of Black Friday, Cyber Monday and open-box sales in India's expanding promotional calendar, and the scale is growing. This year, DLF and Oberoi Malls estimated that around half the brands in their malls would participate in Black Friday promotions, while brands at DLF malls reported sales increases of 20-35% during the event.

title: We Don't Need No 'Sale Day' Reason
